title: Event ID Guidelines and Backwards-compatibility Strategy for Audit Exports (v0.1)
content:
Purpose

This note proposes a compact, implementation-friendly convention for event identifiers and a backwards-compatibility strategy for audit log schema evolution across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. It focuses on enabling robust SIEM exports, reliable evidence linking, and minimal churn for RBAC consumers when we move from v1->v2->v3 of the schema.

Scope

Applies to:
- All server-side produced audit events (API gateway, control plane, serving runtime, console) that flow to the audit pipeline.
- SIEM export formats (JSON-over-kafka and JSON-for-S3 delivery).
- Evidence automation artifacts that reference event IDs (forensic bundles, case files).
Excludes: client telemetry, ephemeral debug logs not retained for compliance.

Design goals

1) Deterministic, stable identifiers that survive routing and re-serialization.
2) Compact form for high-cardinality pipelines and retention-friendly storage.
3) Clear versioning marker so downstream consumers can safely parse/ignore unknown fields.
4) Migration-friendly: allow old parsers to continue to work with new events and vice versa when possible.

Event identifier format (proposal)

We propose a single string field event_id with the following structure (dash-separated):

{env_prefix}-{source}-{epoch_ms}-{seq_hex}-{schema_tag}

Components:
- env_prefix (2–3 chars): production: pr, staging: st, private customer: pc{orgid truncated to 2}. Helps triage mixed-environment exports in aggregated SIEMs.
- source (short token): api, cp (control-plane), srv (serving-runtime), console, ds (dedicated-scheduler)
- epoch_ms: 13-digit epoch milliseconds at event creation time (UTC)
- seq_hex: 6–8 hexadecimal sequence to disambiguate events created in the same ms by the same source instance (wraps at 2^(24 or 32)).
- schema_tag: short schema version marker (v1, v2, v3rc1). This is required for the first message for a given request-context and can be omitted in follow-up child events if the pipeline enriches them with parent_schema_tag.

Example: pr-api-1700053123456-0a3f5b-v1

Rationale: epoch_ms ensures global ordering approximation without external coordination, seq_hex gives low-overhead uniqueness for high-throughput producers, and schema_tag surfaces schema evolution to consumers.

Canonical fields recommended for every audit event

- event_id: string (see format above)
- event_type: short token drawn from central taxonomy (see taxonomy section)
- timestamp: RFC3339 with ns precision (for SIEM-friendly display)
- actor: {principal_id} (string) — the authenticated principal initiating the action
- target: short description or resource_id
- rbac_context: minimal context used by RBAC consumers (role_grant_ids list as comma-delimited string if needed)
- evidence_links: comma-separated list of evidence ids (see evidence section)
- schema: short URI or tag (deprecated in favor of schema_tag in event_id but keep for compatibility)

Event taxonomy (brief)

Categories should be single-token event_type entries. We recommend a top-level namespace and subtype separated by a dot: e.g., policy.change, auth.login, model.deploy, inference.call, billing.charge_attempt. Keep event_type set small and stable; new detailed attributes should be added as optional fields.

Example taxonomy excerpt:
- auth.login
- auth.switch-role
- config.policy.create
- config.policy.update
- model.version.create
- model.deploy.start
- model.deploy.complete
- inference.request.start
- inference.request.finish
- evidence.bundle.create

SIEM export considerations

- Flattening: Downstream SIEMs prefer shallow JSON; exporters should map arrays to comma-delimited strings for fields known to be cardinality-friendly (e.g., evidence_links) and keep nested JSON only for occasional raw_payload.
- Field name stability: Use a small, well-documented set of canonical field names to avoid proliferation (event_id, event_type, timestamp, actor, source_ip, outcome, target, evidence_links, message).
- Schema_tag visibility: Maintain schema_tag in event_id and event.schema for quick filtering on older SIEM queries.
- Sampling / redaction: Provide a top-level flags field for exporters to note sampling (sampled_out=true) and redaction reasons.

RBAC context and producer responsibilities

- Producers must attach a minimal rbac_context token (string) with enough information to map to role grants in a downstream audit view. For privacy, include only IDs, not full grant payloads.
- When a change event affects policy state (config.policy.*), the event MUST include affected_grants: comma-delimited list of grant IDs.

Evidence automation and linking

We distinguish between evidence (artifacts stored for forensics) and audit events (metadata). Evidence items have their own evidence_id: ev-<short-hash>-<epoch_day>. Evidence_links on events reference those IDs. Evidence producers should emit a first-class evidence.create event with: evidence_id, event_id_parent (the audit event that triggered it), storage_uri (S3 path or internal bundle id), checksum, and retention_tier.

Backwards-compatibility and versioning strategy

Principles:
- Non-breaking additive changes are allowed (add new optional fields).
- Renames or type changes are breaking and must be gatekept via schema_tag and rollout phases.
- Consumers should default-ignore unknown fields.

Rollout phases (for a schema bump, e.g., v1->v2):
1) Design and internal preview: create sample events with schema_tag=v2rc1.
2) Dual-write opt-in: for a transition period, producers emit both v1 and v2 formats (one event with a v1 tag and a sibling event with v2_tag) or populate event.alternate_payload with the other format.
3) Exporter shim layer: exporters will translate v2 back to v1 for legacy SIEM consumers using a documented mapping table.
4) Migration window: define a fixed window (e.g., 90 days) during which shims are supported.
5) Deprecation and removal: after the period, drop the shim and increment event_id schema tag required for new events.

Practical compatibility techniques

- Field-presence markers: include fields like "schema_compat: [v1,v1.1]" as a string to quickly indicate expected compatibility.
- Translation catalogs: maintain a mapping CSV that exporters use to map v2 fields to v1 names and types.
- Consumer tests: add unit tests in downstream SIEM parsers that verify they can handle both v1 and v2 samples.

Migration task checklist (v1 -> v2 -> v3)

- [ ] Define v2 field additions and breaking changes with owners.
- [ ] Produce sample payloads for each event_type.
- [ ] Implement dual-write option in 2 pilot producers (api gateway, control plane).
- [ ] Build exporter shim mapping and smoke-test with Splunk team.
- [ ] Notify integrators and partner customers with export change notices (Confluence + email).
- [ ] Run 90-day migration window and gather telemetry on parsing errors.

Open questions and trade-offs

1) How to handle private tenant IDs in event_id when customers require stronger isolation? Proposal: for private deployments skip env_prefix and include pc-<tenant_hash2>. Need legal review.
2) Should we move to a UUIDv6 style event id instead of epoch+seq to rely on standard libraries? Trade-off: readability and chronological sorting vs standardization.
3) How aggressive should exporter shims be? Translating complex nested objects is error-prone; recommend shims only for flat renames and small type conversions.

Appendix: short examples

Example event (v1 style):
{
  event_id: "pr-api-1700053123456-0a3f5b-v1",
  event_type: "inference.request.start",
  timestamp: "2024-02-15T19:45:23.456Z",
  actor: "user_akapoor",
  target: "model:gpt-open-8b:rev-202402",
  rbac_context: "grant_197,grant_198",
  evidence_links: "ev-9f23a-20240215"
}

Example evidence.create event:
{
  event_id: "pr-ds-1700053123460-00fc21-v1",
  event_type: "evidence.bundle.create",
  evidence_id: "ev-9f23a-20240215",
  event_id_parent: "pr-api-1700053123456-0a3f5b-v1",
  storage_uri: "s3://redwood-forensics/prod/bundles/ev-9f23a-20240215.tar.gz",
  checksum: "sha256:2b7e...",
  retention_tier: "7y:compliance"
}

Next steps

- Review with serving-runtime, control-plane, and SRE teams (owners listed in collaborators).
- Approve canonical taxonomy list (separate doc) and publish a translation CSV for initial shim.
- Begin pilot dual-write on staging for two weeks and collect parsing error metrics.

Notes to reviewers

I intentionally kept event_type compact and pushed richer contextual attributes to optional fields to minimize downstream schema churn. Please flag any mandatory consumer needs that require moving additional attributes from optional -> required.

-- Aisha K. (on behalf of Security & Compliance)
